claims.text: An on-the-fly trained machine-learning interatomic potential combined with enhanced sampling and thermodynamic integration can replace explicit ab initio molecular dynamics for phase free-energy evaluation.
The proposed workflow can accurately capture solid and liquid free energies near fusion.
The proposed workflow can retain anharmonic vibrational contributions to free energy.
The proposed workflow can retain electronic and electron–vibration contributions to free energy.
The proposed workflow will cost at least an order of magnitude less than explicit ab initio free-energy molecular dynamics.
The proposed workflow will scale better than TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems.
Training the machine-learning potential on targeted ab initio data can incorporate electron–vibration coupling and anharmonic effects.
Enhanced sampling and thermodynamic integration along a phase-transition pathway can recover free energies and entropy contributions for both phases.
Reproducing ab initio forces and energies with a machine-learning potential will preserve the fidelity of free-energy differences across phase transitions.
Replacing most explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics sampling with the machine-learning potential will reduce computational cost.
The cost advantage should be especially large in complex multicomponent systems where TOR-TILD becomes inefficient.
Fusion free energies and phase-transition properties will agree with explicit ab initio molecular dynamics within a few percent.
The workflow will reduce computational cost by 10–100 times relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The workflow will provide higher throughput than TOR-TILD in multicomponent systems.
Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics free-energy calculations provide high accuracy at high computational cost.
TOR-TILD provides high accuracy for elemental and binary systems at high computational cost.
The method is expected to remain valid from elemental and binary systems through high-entropy alloys containing at least five elements.
The method is expected to remain valid from temperatures near melting into the fully molten regime.
